open-question.question: The project-wide principle store stands at `milestones/answer_decision_principles.md`, inside the root `milestones/` container, which no longer exists once a mission stands directly in its scope as `mission_<slug>/`. The recommendation pass reads the store and the capture skill writes it at one fixed path both name literally, so it needs a path that depends on no mission. At what path does the principle store live after the rename?

Some occurrences of the word milestone stay by decision after the rename (the CHANGELOG's entries, the `milestone_NN` directory names and the numbered milestones `CLAUDE.md` cites for its measurements), so a search that finds nothing cannot be the bar, and the test suites pin behaviour, not vocabulary: a leftover in runtime prose, in the docs, or in a help text no test quotes fails nothing. How is the rename known to be complete: by a listed residue a test checks, by a listed residue checked once by hand when the work ends, or by no bar beyond the drift gate and the suites?

This milestone stands at `milestones/rename-milestone-to-mission/`, and the skills that work on it are served from the working tree's `hosts/claude`, which the rename's own tasks rebuild under the new word; from that rebuild on, that copy takes no `--milestone` flag, discovers nothing under a `milestones/` container, and writes `Mission-finish:`. Two choices constrain each other here. Which copy of the plugin runs this milestone's own tasks and its finish: a copy held at the old word for the length of the work, or the working tree's, with the rebuild that switches it held to the last task? And how is the milestone itself finished: where it stands, as the last `Milestone-finish:` commit, which the renamed tool never prints, or moved to `mission_rename-milestone-to-mission/` and finished as the first `Mission-finish:` commit?

A second live milestone, `milestones/rename-cairn-to-gurita/`, defined and not started, stands in the root `milestones/` container, where the renamed plugin discovers nothing, while this work is to end with `main` consistent under the new word. How does that milestone come to stand under the new form: is its directory moved to `mission_rename-cairn-to-gurita/` as part of this work, is it defined again by the renamed plugin, or is it left where it stands for its own work to deal with?

The bootstrap skill writes the workflow section into the context file only when the file holds no section under that section's heading, which the rename changes from `## Milestone Workflow` to `## Mission Workflow`, and with `/migrate-milestones` removed no skill rewrites an older section. What does the bootstrap do with a context file that holds a `## Milestone Workflow` section and no `## Mission Workflow` one: append the new section and leave the old one standing beside it, replace the old section with the new one, or stop?

`/migrate-milestones` is the only caller of the commit tool's `--date` option, which sets a commit's author date and is covered by `tests/test_commit_date.py`. When the skill is removed, is the option removed from the tool together with its test, or kept with no caller?
open-question.alternative: The `--date` option is removed from `core/tools/commit.py` in the same work that removes `/migrate-milestones`: its parser entry, `check_date`, the `--date DATE` arguments added to `git commit`, and the three usage lines, docstring paragraph, and help text that state it. `tests/test_commit_date.py` is deleted, `--date` is dropped from the option set `tests/test_commit_contract.py` asserts (and from that test's name), and the option's mentions in `CLAUDE.md`'s committing invariant and in `docs/workflow.md` go with it, with no entry banning its return. The rebuilt host trees carry the reduced tool byte-identical, as the parity test requires. The tool's contract then states only what some caller uses, in keeping with a hard cut that keeps nothing of the old vocabulary's machinery, and an author-date input whose only reason for existing was re-finishing pointer-era history is not left for a later reader or runner to wonder about or pass; the option is 23 lines of the tool and a whole test file that no longer need maintaining or renaming. It widens a rename milestone into a behavioural change of a tool that otherwise changes only in its docstrings and help text, adding edits to the tool, two test files, and the invariant; and if a later need to backdate commits arises (a re-finish or backfill of some other record), the option and its tests have to be written again rather than found in place.

The `--date` option and `tests/test_commit_date.py` stay as they are, with no removal planned, and the contract test's option set is unchanged; only the prose that gives `/migrate-milestones` as its reason (`CLAUDE.md`'s committing invariant, `docs/workflow.md`) is reworded to describe it as an author-date input that no skill passes, as part of removing the skill's mentions. It is the smallest change: the tool and its tests stay untouched apart from the rename's own wording, the option remains tested and costs nothing at run time (a call without it runs exactly the commands it ran before), and it stays available should a later piece of work need to keep an original date on a commit it makes. The commit tool keeps a documented, tested option that nothing in the plugin calls, which runs against the hard cut's removal of what existed only for the migration, leaves its help text and the invariant describing a capability with no use, and keeps a 300-line test file maintained for it.

open-question.question: The read-only tool strips a legacy `Milestone <N>: ` prefix from the title it reads off a `requirements.md` heading, and the finish skill strips the same prefix from the title line of its commit body. No directory defined under the new word carries that prefix, and the hard cut reads nothing recorded under the old vocabulary. Is the prefix strip removed with the rename, or kept as it is?

The read-only tool's `tasks PATH` query lists every `Task-completion:` commit that changed PATH and joins each to its milestone through the discovery pattern, printing a fixed placeholder in the milestone field when the commit's task list matches none. `Task-completion:` does not carry the word and stays, so after the rename every one of the 233 task commits already in the log is such an unmatched commit. Does `tasks` go on listing them under the placeholder, with their verified bars under `--with-body`, or does the record's start at the rename leave them out?

`ideas/` holds three design drafts that carry the word milestone 189 times between them: `ideas/gurita.md`, the dated draft this rename follows, whose tables state the old forms as what stands today, `ideas/kepala.md`, and `ideas/benchmark_for_cairn.md`. Do the drafts follow the rename, or stay as written?

The hard cut gives an existing project no migration: a live milestone under a `milestones/` container and the pointer-era state release 1.9.0 left (`milestones/README.md`, numbered directories) are read by nothing in the renamed plugin. Does the documentation this work rewrites say what such a project does at the upgrade, such as finishing its live milestones first or moving a directory by hand, or does it describe only the new shape and leave the upgrade to the release notes written by the plugin rename's work?

The on-demand host suite is owed a passing run against each host whose trigger set a change touches, and this rename touches all three hosts' sets: slot value files and README templates in each host's definition, `core/agents/*.md`, and `host_tests/` itself. The plugin rename that follows directly touches the same sets again. Is the host suite run and passed on all three hosts within this work, or is that run left to the plugin rename's work?

The principle store's text is written only by the capture skill, and it carries the word milestone on three lines: its header names `capture-milestone-principle-updates` as the file's only writer, one principle's origin line cites `MILESTONE_DIR` and an earlier question's title, and one principle's text speaks of the milestone record. Does this work edit the store's text by hand so it follows the rename, or leave the text as written until a capture run rewrites it?

`CLAUDE.md` records the design decisions a later editor must not undo, often by naming a retired form with a ban on restoring it. Does it gain such an entry for the hard cut, naming the retired forms (the `milestones/` container, the `--milestone` flag, the `Milestone-definition:` and `Milestone-finish:` markers, `/migrate-milestones`) as never to be accepted or read again, which keeps the old word in the file by decision, or does it describe only the new shape?
